cards.summary: SQL grouping or aggregation work can require aggregation or temporary-work resources and is distinct from a lock primitive.
source_refs: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual: optimization and temporary-table execution

cards.summary: A runtime type conversion in a predicate or join can make a selective condition non-sargable and increase access work; it is not a lock primitive.
source_refs: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual: optimization and index use

cards.summary: An absent useful index can make a selective predicate use a broad access path and increase query work; it is not a lock primitive.
source_refs: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual: optimization and index use

cards.summary: Transaction or row-lock contention blocks work and causes lock waits. It can coexist with an independent query-work mechanism.
source_refs: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual: Performance Schema data_lock_waits

cards.summary: An absent useful index can make a selective predicate use a broad access path and increase query work; it is not a lock primitive.
source_refs: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual: optimization and index use

cards.summary: Ordering or sorting work can require sort or temporary-work resources and is distinct from a lock primitive.
source_refs: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual: optimization and filesort

cards.summary: A broad full-table read or scan increases read and execution work but is not a lock primitive.
source_refs: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual: optimization and table scans

cards.summary: An overly large multi-table join can increase cardinality and join work; it is not a lock primitive.
source_refs: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual: optimization and nested-loop joins

cards.summary: Conflicting record updates or transactions create lock contention. It can coexist with an independent read or query-work mechanism.
source_refs: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual: InnoDB locking and Performance Schema data_lock_waits

cards.summary: Physical table or relation bloat increases storage and scan overhead and is distinct from direct lock contention.
source_refs: Database operations reference: table and relation storage bloat
